title: Graceful traffic attenuation and rollback playbook for LTS-aware progressive upgrades
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Define and implement a telemetry-driven attenuation layer and rollback playbook to safely promote runtime-2.4 to LTS and to handle surge, regression signals, and downstream consumer affinity during progressive delivery.
proposal_summary: Introduce a mid-path attenuation controller that sits between the traffic router and rollout orchestrator. The controller will compute a real-time attenuation score using SLO deltas, error spikes, tail latency, and quality regressions from evaluation hooks. Based on thresholds, the controller will (1) progressively reduce traffic to the new version, (2) apply per-customer affinity bypasses for LTS channels, and (3) trigger automated soft-rollback actions (traffic caps, degradation to lightweight model variant, or full rollback).
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry pipeline surfaces 90th/99th latency, error-rate deltas, and quality-regression score within 20s of occurrence.
Attenuation controller can apply traffic reduction to a cohort in <30s and restore within <60s after signal clears.
Automated rollback triggers must be configurable per-release and tested in staging with injected fault scenarios.
Can perform single-command mitigation that drops new-version load to 0% or routes to fallback model variant with no manual configuration changes.
Playbook documented and validated with runbook steps for on-call, including alert thresholds and escalation contacts.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22 - Diego Martinez: Kickoff meeting; agreed scope: attenuation controller + playbook + staging chaos tests. Action: design doc draft assigned to Maya.

2026-02-28 - Maya Chen: Initial design doc posted to Confluence; major decision: use blended score (SLODelta*3 + ErrorRate*2 + QualityRegressions*5) as the primary signal. Seeking feedback from Observability and SRE.

2026-03-03 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Reviewed design; asked to add circuit-breaker hysteresis to avoid flapping during transient spikes. Identified two Datadog alerts to reuse: runtime-requests-err-rate and runtime-tail-latency.
2026-03-06 - Maya Chen: Prototype attenuation service created (k8s deployment) and smoke-tested in staging. Prototype exposes /attenuate API and accepts JSON signal payloads. PR opened: #412.

2026-03-09 - QA Lead Priya Sharma: Started chaos tests in staging injecting latency and error spikes; observed controller applied a 40% attenuation after 18s for sustained 99th latency spike. Recording suggests threshold tuning required to avoid overreaction to short-lived spikes.
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: Adjusted scoring weights and added 60s cooldown window per cohort. Updated acceptance criteria and notified on-call.
review_feedback: SRE (Arjun Patel): Add per-region and per-tenant attenuation caps and an opt-out flag for emergency LTS customers.
Observability (Nadia Park): Ensure the attenuation score is visible in the rollout dashboard with a historical trail for incident postmortems.
Product (Leah O'Connor): Feature flagging model affinity must ensure LTS-marked customer routes are stable; do not switch LTS traffic without explicit opt-in.
implementation_notes: Controller runs as low-latency sidecar-eligible service; decisions published to the router via xDS-style config and persisted in rollout CRD annotations.
Fallback actions prioritized: 1) apply attenuation (percent traffic reduction), 2) switch cohorts to fallback model variant, 3) enact full rollback.
Rollback scoring combines severity (magnitude of SLO breach), velocity (rate of change), and coverage (percent of traffic affected) to avoid noisy triggers. Thresholds are tunable per-release.
Will reuse existing rollout CRD (no schema change) but add attenuationStatus and lastDecisionTime fields as annotations for traceability.
risks: Risk of oscillation if attenuation cooldown not tuned leading to repeated partial rollbacks.
Potential for LTS customer churn if routing changes accidentally affect opt-in cohorts; mitigated via explicit per-customer opt-out/opt-in flags.
Telemetry gaps: events that happen faster than our aggregation window could be missed; need to reduce aggregation window for critical metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for score computation and hysteresis logic.
Staging canary: simulate 3 failure modes (latency spike, error-rate surge, eval-quality regression) against a 10k rps synthetic workload.
Chaos test: network latency + node kill during mid-ramp, assert attenuation engages and no LTS cohort loses >= 1% availability.
Post-deploy: 48h observation with automated garment checks to ensure no regression on cost-per-token.
next_steps: Finish PR #412 review and merge (Maya) - target 2026-03-12.
Add per-tenant opt-in flag and adjust rollout UI to expose attenuation slider (ENG-82610).
Schedule on-call drill with SRE to practice manual rollback and one-button mitigation (2026-03-17).
Finalize runbook and escalate path; create PagerDuty play and update on-call rotation with escalation contacts.
notes: This initiative is a bridge between release engineering and SRE: runtime-2.4 is a candidate LTS and needs extra safeguards during promotion.
Keep the controller lightweight; prefer routing-based mitigations over heavy-handed DB migrations.
